Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. Senegal now has two active, verifiable IXPs in Dakar rather than one: SENIX (Packet Clearing House, established 2017) and HubSIX (PeeringDB and Internet Society Pulse, 5 peers, 6 connections, 60 Gbps total capacity, with route servers carrying 10-20 Gbps ports). This is active IXP(s) with moderate participation rather than a single limited-participation exchange; revised to code 4.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. The cited figure (22.4 million SIM connections, 123% of population) measures connections, which the variable definition explicitly excludes since a person can hold multiple SIMs. GSMA's own December 2025 analysis, reported by Ecofin Agency, estimates around 9.9 million unique mobile subscribers in 2025, or nearly 52% of the population, which falls in the 40-54% band. Revised to code 3.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Regional cloud availability zone nearby (same sub-region)
Comments: Regional zones (JNB GCP), local sovereign init [Ecofin](https://www.ecofinagency.com/telecom/0410-45971-senegal-launches-sovereign-cloud-initiative-with-google)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. AWS announced general availability of an AWS Wavelength Zone in Dakar in April 2025, in partnership with Sonatel (Orange), independently confirmed by Telecompaper as the first Wavelength Zone in West Africa. This is a genuine local edge node from a major hyperscaler, not merely a distant regional zone; revised to code 4 (at least one major provider with local presence or edge node). The Google sovereign cloud remains at MOU stage and does not by itself change this.

Definition: The country's overall cybersecurity preparedness, based on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI). Covers legal measures, technical measures, organisational measures, capacity development, and cooperation. Essential for trust in stored data and digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. The originally cited score of 51.61 does not match the actual ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 result: Ecofin Agency and an independent statistics site both report Senegal's GCI 2024 score as 67.17-67.34, which falls in the 60-79 (Advancing) band under this project's scale, not 40-59 (Establishing). Note that ITU's own qualitative tier label for Senegal is Tier 3, which does not map neatly onto the numeric bands used here; flagging this label/score tension, but recalculating strictly against the numeric scale gives code 4.

revision_notes: Confirmed and better sourced. DataCenterMap lists 7 small facilities from 3 operators (Sonatel, ONIX, STELLARIX). Definition: Whether the government has established dedicated data center infrastructure and/or a government cloud (G-Cloud) strategy for hosting e-government services and public sector data domestically. Critical for data sovereignty and e-government service delivery.
Value Name: National data center operational with cloud strategy adopted
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and better sourced. Senegal's national Diamniadio data centre, run by state operator SENUM (formerly ADIE), has been operational since 2021 and hosts government and some private-sector data, with a sovereign cloud strategy advancing under the New Deal Technologique (operational phase launched March 2026). Code 4 is well supported beyond the single Google MOU originally cited.

Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. The cited World Bank figure itself (74.2%, 2023) falls just below the 75% threshold and sits within the 50-74% band, not 75-89% as coded; GOGLA's country brief corroborates with a 70.4% national electrification rate. Some national sources (e.g. IEA citing Senegal's Ministry of Petroleum and Energy) report a higher figure of around 85% for 2021, so this is flagged for human review, but the World Bank data specified in the metadata's primary sources supports code 3.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Senegal's official universal access programme, led by ASER and ANER, combines grid extension, mini-grid and decentralised solar rollouts targeting 100% coverage by 2025, and is co-financed by the Green Climate Fund's ASER Solar Rural Electrification Project; this is a comprehensive framework with significant deployment, supporting code 4.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and re-sourced with the correct metric. The original source cited installed capacity, not generation. IEA's Senegal 2023 Energy Policy Review states renewables (mainly solar and wind) accounted for around 21% of generation in 2022, and a more recent IRENA-based estimate reported by Ecofin puts 2024 generation share at 15% (25% of capacity); both remain within the 10-24% band, so code 2 stands.

Both fall within the 21-40pp band, so code 3 stands.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
Value Name: Developing (growing startup base, regular funding rounds, several hubs)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. The original source discussed a pan-African fund, not Senegal-specific data. Partech's 2025 Africa Tech VC report shows Senegal raised about US$84M in equity (+137% YoY, 10 deals) and US$223M including debt (+449% YoY), one of only three markets outside the big four to clear the US$50M equity threshold, alongside Wave (Africa's first Francophone unicorn), a dedicated Startup Act, and multiple hubs and accelerators such as CTIC Dakar and Jokkolabs. This meets the Established threshold; revised to code 4.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The originally cited figure of 15 hubs (2019 Briter Bridges/AfriLabs data) would itself map to the 10-24 band, inconsistent with the code 3 that was selected, so it did not properly support the score either way. A World Bank tech-hub inventory and current hub websites identify a smaller set of consistently active, named hubs in Senegal (CTIC Dakar, Jokkolabs Dakar, Africa Living Lab, Jiguene Tech Hub, Mobile Senegal, plus newer university-based living labs in Ziguinchor and at the digital university), which better supports the 3-9 hub band. Code 3 confirmed on fresher evidence, though the original citation was internally inconsistent.

Definition: The size and vibrancy of the local software developer and technology professional community. Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Indicates the country's capacity to build and maintain digital systems locally.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. The cited figure of 912 GitHub users is itself below the 1,000 threshold needed for code 3 (Developing), so the original source did not support its own score. A second, independent GitHub statistics tool corroborates a similarly small count (200 users). Both proxies point to Emerging rather than Developing, though such trackers likely undercount the true developer population and no Stack Overflow, Octoverse or Google Developer Group country-level data could be found to corroborate a higher band; revised to code 2 with residual uncertainty noted.

Definition: The country's e-government development level based on the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI). This composite index measures online service delivery, telecommunications infrastructure, and human capital. Indicates the government's capacity to deliver digital public services.
redteam_note: Source is a dev/aggregator/off-topic domain — check it actually supports the score. Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and re-sourced. The official UN DESA E-Government Survey 2024 gives Senegal an EGDI of 0.5162, noting the country moved from the Middle to the High EGDI group between 2022 and 2024; this replaces the weak, off-topic HSE University blog originally cited and confirms code 3 (EGDI 0.50-0.64), with the year updated to 2024.

Definition: The scale and quality of tertiary-level ICT and STEM education programmes available in the country, based on the number and quality of institutions offering ICT degrees, computer science programmes, and engineering courses relative to the population.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Score confirmed but source replaced. The originally cited ichei.org page is a Chinese UNESCO-ICHEI partner directory listing a single university and is mislabelled as UNESCO; it only weakly supports the score. Better evidence, including Universite Gaston Berger's long-running Master en Informatique/2ITIC programme and Supdeco Dakar's computer engineering bachelor's degree, confirms several institutions offer ICT programmes with growing enrolment, consistent with Moderate. No quantitative UNESCO STEM-graduate percentage for Senegal was found, so recommend human review to firm up the evidentiary base.
